You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testExtremeValues()` exercises the cumulativeProbability method of NormalDistributionImpl with very large and very small input values, including going up to 100 in both positive and negative direction, and also tests the extremes like Double.MAX_VALUE. The failure arises because the cumulativeProbability method internally calls Erf.erf() which can throw MaxIterationsExceededException, a subtype of ConvergenceException, indicating that the underlying error function calculation failed to converge for some inputs.

Inspecting NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability(double x) reveals its implementation. It computes the standardized deviation dev = x - mean and then returns cumulative probability as 0.5 * (1 + Erf.erf(dev / (standardDeviation * sqrt(2)))). The call to Erf.erf() is wrapped in a try-catch block that catches MaxIterationsExceededException. On catching, it attempts to handle extreme values by returning 0 (if x is much less than mean - 20 standard deviations) or 1 (if x is much greater than mean + 20 standard deviations). If x is within these bounds, the exception is thrown further.

The test likely triggers the exception for large magnitude parameters outside the specified cutoff range or for extreme values like infinity for which the Erf implementation cannot compute. This leads to the exception bubbling up as a ConvergenceException during the test, causing a failure.

In particular, the test currently allows i up to 100 but the threshold for catching and mapping to 0/1 is only set at mean ± 20 standard deviations, so for values between 20 and 100 standard deviations from the mean (which the test exercises), the exception is thrown instead of returning a limit value, causing the failure.

Hence, the root cause is that the current handling of MaxIterationsExceededException in NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability only returns boundary values at +/- 20 standard deviations, but the test goes beyond this, expecting the method to handle these extreme inputs gracefully without throwing exceptions.

No recent bug reports appear related; only this one reports convergence exceptions on large inputs.

Therefore, the failure is due to insufficient range handling of the exception in cumulativeProbability. The fix would be to either increase the cutoff threshold (e.g., to 100), or better handle very large values including positive/negative infinity, to avoid propagation of MaxIterationsExceededException for inputs in the extended range tested. Additionally, the test comment hints that some conditions are temporarily limited due to known issues (MATH-364), indicating that the current code is a workaround.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
